levelDescription.pastoral: Sufficient for pastoral preaching with solid biblical grounding — not designed for academic work.

sourceTypeRelationships.lexiconWithTheologicalDict: Technical lexicons (BDAG/HALOT) and theological dictionaries (TDNT/NIDNTTE) complement, not substitute, each other: the lexicon gives raw morpho-semantic data on the term; the theological dictionary traces its use across the canon. If your corpus is constrained, prioritize the technical lexicon.
sourceTypeRelationships.lexiconWithGrammar: The lexicon covers the lexical level (words); the grammar covers the sentence level (syntax). Together they cover the original verse by verse.
sourceTypeRelationships.theologicalDictWithLexicon: The theological dictionary brings canonical trajectory of the term; the lexicon (BDAG/HALOT) brings raw lemma data. If your corpus is constrained, the technical lexicon is more foundational for exegesis.
sourceTypeRelationships.criticalWithExpository: Critical commentaries (WBC/NIGTC) detail syntax and textual criticism; expository ones (NICOT/BECNT) emphasize theology and application. They cover distinct angles of the same text — serious work usually requires both.
sourceTypeRelationships.expositoryWithCritical: Expository commentaries give you the finished theological reading; critical commentaries show the technical decisions behind it. Both contribute to the same verse from different planes.
sourceTypeRelationships.backgroundWithPrimary: Modern syntheses (deSilva, Keener IVP) save time; primary sources (Josephus, Philo, Apostolic Fathers) give voice to the ancient witness directly. One without the other leaves gaps.
sourceTypeRelationships.primaryWithBackground: Ancient primary sources (Josephus, Philo, OTP) are the direct witnesses of the text's world; modern syntheses (deSilva, Keener IVP) contextualize and interpret them. Both are needed.

plan.rubricEmpty: The rubric has no emphasis for this step. Pick the types that fit your paper.

rubricJustification.introduction: The introduction presents the thesis and positions the passage. Your voice leads: historical-cultural context and theological positioning support it, and technical analysis (lexicon, grammar, critical apparatus) belongs in the body.
rubricJustification.verse: Verse-by-verse work is where the dialectical method is fully exercised. The three voices dialogue: the anchor (base reading), the contrasts (other critical/theological voice), and the technical apparatus (lexicon, grammar, critical) that defends each decision.
rubricJustification.conclusion: The conclusion synthesizes the findings into a coherent theological reading. It's your voice integrating the work: commentaries and monographs scaffold the synthesis — no new voices are introduced and no critical debates are opened.

compose.title: Compose academic paper
compose.subtitle: We generate TMS-style academic prose from the accepted canonical analyses of each verse. The configured style guide is mandatorily applied.
compose.idleBody: The canonical analyses of each verse are turned into a continuous academic paper: introduction + verse-by-verse body + conclusion + bibliography. Citations follow the configured style guide.
compose.cost: Each composition uses one Gemini Pro 2.5 call with extended context. Review the result and press "Save to paper" to keep it: otherwise it is lost on close.
compose.composingBody: This may take 30 to 120 seconds depending on verse count and analysis density.
compose.formatterApplied: Style guide applied (step 1: instructions to the assistant, step 2: automatic reformat).
compose.formatterSkipped: You haven't extracted the style guide into structured rules yet. Only step 1 (instructions to the assistant) was applied. Go to the "Style guide" tab and extract the guide to activate step 2.
compose.formatterError: Error during the automatic reformat. The assistant's composition is still valid.

dialog.title: Coherence review
dialog.description: A single Gemini pass over the entire accepted paper to surface inconsistencies between introduction, verses, and conclusion.
dialog.idleBody: The reviewer reads ALL accepted sections (introduction + verses + conclusion) and returns verifiable problems only. No praise, no summaries.
dialog.cost: One Gemini Pro 2.5 call (~$0.05–0.15 depending on paper length).
